title: Landscape visual evaluation and place attachment in historical and cultural districts: a study based on semantic differential scale and eye tracking experimental methods
study_aim: To investigate the relationships between Visual Attention (VA), demographic influences, and perceived landscape values (Aesthetic Value and Cultural Value) in historical and cultural districts, using a dual-method approach combining Eye-Tracking (ET) technology and Semantic Differential (SD) scale.
hypotheses: H1: VA Correlates with AV and CV Assessments: Areas within the landscapes that attract higher VA, as measured by ET data, will be rated higher in AV and CV assessments in the SD questionnaire.

H2: Demographic Variables Influence Perception of Landscape Values: Demographic factors such as age, gender, and nationality significantly influence how participants assess the AV and CV of the landscapes.

H3: Cultural Features Attract Less Immediate VA but Higher Value Ratings: Cultural features within the landscapes may attract less immediate VA (later fixation in gaze plots) but will receive higher value ratings for historical depth and cultural integrity in the SD questionnaire.

H4: Natural Features Generate More Immediate VA: Natural features of the landscapes, such as mountains and water features in Jade Dragon Snow Mountain, will attract more immediate VA (earlier fixation in gaze plots) compared to building or cultural elements.

participants.recruitment_method: Stratified sampling from popular spots within Lijiang Old Town and Jade Dragon Snow Mountain.

environmental_features.description: Towering mountains, water features, natural scenery.
Ancient Naxi civilization, Daoist influences, historical architecture, cultural traits and practices.

environmental_features.location: Lijiang Old Town, Jade Dragon Snow Mountain
environmental_features.description: Facilities and infrastructures designed to accommodate tourists.

measures.name: Visual Attention (VA)
metrics: Initial Gaze Points (GP) / Number of Fixation Points (NF)
Gaze Movement Patterns (GMP) / Number of Visits (NV)

analysis_methods: Statistical tests (F-values), Pearson correlation coefficients, Cronbach's alpha, Average Variance Extracted (AVE), Composite Reliability (CR), test-retest reliability.

concept_definitions.name: Visual Attention (VA)
concept_definitions.definition: Objective measures of where participants first focus their attention, how long their gaze remains fixed, and the sequence and path of eye movements across an image, reflecting interest and cognitive processing.

concept_definitions.name: Semantic Differential (SD) scale
concept_definitions.definition: A questionnaire-based method using a five-point Likert scale to quantitatively measure subjective assessments of landscape values and visitor experiences.

concept_definitions.name: Aesthetic Value (AV)
concept_definitions.definition: The perceived beauty and visual appeal of a landscape, encompassing scenic integrity, ecological vitality, visual comfort, distinctiveness, and ambiance.

concept_definitions.name: Cultural Value (CV)
concept_definitions.definition: The perceived historical, social, and traditional significance of a landscape, including historical depth, cultural integrity, symbolic resonance, narrative coherence, and conservation commitment.

concept_definitions.name: Place Attachment (PA)
concept_definitions.definition: The emotional and psychological bond individuals feel towards a specific place, reflecting resonance with heritage, sense of belonging, and memories.

concept_definitions.name: Nature Engagement (NE)
concept_definitions.definition: The extent to which individuals feel connected to and fascinated by the natural environment, including flora, fauna, and natural settings.

concept_definitions.name: Architectural Appeal (AA)
concept_definitions.definition: The perceived attractiveness and historical significance of architectural features within a landscape, influencing ambiance and attention.

concept_definitions.name: Number of Fixation Points (NF)
concept_definitions.definition: An eye-tracking metric recording where participants first focus their attention upon viewing images, indicating initial visual appeal.

concept_definitions.name: Total Fixation Duration (TFD)
concept_definitions.definition: An eye-tracking metric measuring the total time participants' gaze remains fixed on a particular image element, reflecting depth of cognitive processing and sustained interest.

concept_definitions.name: Number of Visits (NV)
concept_definitions.definition: An eye-tracking metric tracking the number of revisits to specific areas within an image, indicating sustained interest.

concept_definitions.name: Total Glance Duration (TGD)
concept_definitions.definition: An eye-tracking metric reflecting the overall duration of visual engagement with specific landscape features.

limitations: Laboratory environment for ET reduces ecological validity compared to real-life interactions; future research should use more dynamic and complete environments like virtual reality.
Findings cannot be generalized to different cultural and historically significant areas as the study focused solely on two specific locations.

The study demonstrates correlations but does not investigate the underlying reasons or causal mechanisms triggering these relationships; future research should employ experimental methods to change specific landscape features and measure resulting impacts.
future_research: Use longitudinal approaches to track changes in the relationship between people and landscapes.
Implement more dynamic and complete environments (e.g., virtual reality) for ET studies to better represent real-life tourist experiences.
Increase the study's aim and involve multiple locations with distinct cultural, historical, and natural environments to generalize findings.
Employ experimental methods to change specific landscape features and measure the resulting impacts to comprehend the relationship between VA and valuation better.

paper_metadata.crossref_journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: Abstract:  Adaptation in the face of potentially stressful challenges involves activation of neural, neuroendocrine and neuroendocrine‐immune mechanisms. This has been called “allostasis” or “stability through change” by Sterling and Eyer (Fisher S., Reason J. (eds): Handbook of Life Stress, Cognition and Health. J. Wiley Ltd. 1988, p. 631), and allostasis is an essential component of maintaining homeostasis. When these adaptive systems are turned on and turned off again efficiently and not too frequently, the body is able to cope effectively with challenges that it might not otherwise survive. However, there are a number of circumstances in which allostatic systems may either be overstimulated or not perform normally, and this condition has been termed “allostatic load” or the price of adaptation (McEwen and Stellar, Arch. Int. Med. 1993; 153:2093.). Allostatic load can lead to disease over long periods. Types of allostatic load include (1) frequent activation of allostatic systems; (2) failure to shut off allostatic activity after stress; (3) inadequate response of allostatic systems leading to elevated activity of other, normally counter‐regulated allostatic systems after stress. Examples will be given for each type of allostatic load from research pertaining to autonomic, CNS, neuroendocrine, and immune system activity. The relationship of allostatic load to genetic and developmental predispositions to disease is also considered.
